mappings.note: Lists the forms of government - democracy, monarchy, theocracy, dictatorship, oligarchy. The goal covers the working of democracy and its institutions; none of its LOs reaches a taxonomy of government types, so the goal is the honest code.

India as a parliamentary democracy, with the executive drawn from and answerable to the legislature. The institutions-and-processes clause of the goal; not LO-179, because no election procedure is described.
Three reasons an independent judiciary matters. An institution of democracy, so the goal; LO-178 concerns local versus State government, which this is not.
Argues democracy's superiority through equality, protected rights and accountability - the significance of equality in a democracy. Not the bare goal, because the reasoning rests on equal rights.
Matches four practices to democracy, theocracy, monarchy and dictatorship. A taxonomy item; equality before the law is only one of the four clues, so LO-175 would overstate it.
Finding out what type of government Bhutan, Nepal, Bangladesh and South Africa have. Comparative government under the goal.
Hurdles to democratic ideals - corruption, elite influence, weakened institutions - and how citizens can counter them. The working of democracy, so the goal.
Separates democracy from monarchy and dictatorship by where power comes from. A comparison of government types under the goal.

Kautilya's raksha, palana and yogakshema cited for what a government is for. The item is about the purpose of government, so the civics goal rather than LO-170, which is about a kingdom's own administrative measures.
Sorts real functions of a modern government from controlling personal choices. Functions of government under the goal.
Defines democracy as rule by the people. The foundational concept of the chapter, and squarely the goal's subject.
The legislative function as law-making. An organ of government, so the goal; LO-179 would need the election of that legislature.
Completes Lincoln's definition of democracy. A statement about what democracy is for, so the goal rather than the equality outcome.
The source of authority as the real difference between government types. Comparative government under the goal.
Defines a constitution as the fundamental rules and structures of a state. The constitutional-values clause of the goal.

Universal adult franchise - every adult voting regardless of gender, race or wealth - is the clearest expression of equality in a democracy. Not LO-179, which is about the mechanics of an assembly election rather than the principle of equal suffrage.
Citizens ruling directly against citizens choosing representatives. A distinction between democratic forms under the goal.

Rajadharma read as an ethical limit on a king's power, which the chapter uses to think about accountable rule. Not LO-170, because the item draws a general lesson about authority rather than analysing a kingdom's administration.

Presidential systems electing the executive directly against parliamentary ones electing the legislature. Institutions and processes under the goal; not LO-179, because two systems are compared rather than one procedure described.
Matches the three organs to their work, keyed on the judiciary. Institutions of government under the goal.
Universal franchise, protected rights and an independent judiciary have to be recognised as democracy. A whole-system identification, so the goal rather than the single equality outcome.
Rejects hereditary succession as a democratic principle while keeping equality, freedom and elections. Comparative government under the goal.
The school committee chosen by vote as the most democratic method. Democracy in practice at the most local level, which the goal covers; LO-179 is about elections to a legislative assembly.
The Uttaramerur inscriptions recording elections to a village sabha. The goal explicitly reaches democratic processes at the local level, which is where this early self-government example belongs.
Sorts the real features of the Uttaramerur election - ballot pots, qualifications, dismissal for corruption - from universal adult suffrage. Local democratic process under the goal.
Matches government types to their defining features, keyed on absolute monarchy. Comparative government.
Saudi Arabia as the example of an absolute monarchy. A comparative-government recall under the goal.
Nominal versus real monarchical power in constitutional and absolute monarchies. Comparative government under the goal.
Switzerland as the example of direct-democracy practice. Comparative government under the goal.
Accountability as the government being answerable to the people. A working principle of representative democracy.

The five-year cycle of Lok Sabha general elections is a fact about the electoral process, which LO-179 covers. The outcome names the legislative assembly, but this is the same electoral machinery at the national level.
Ministers resigning on losing the confidence of the Lok Sabha. The working of a parliamentary executive, so the goal rather than the election outcome.
The executive as the branch that implements laws and administers the country. An organ of government under the goal.
Parliament as India's legislature. An institution of Indian democracy, so the goal.
Separation of powers as the independent functioning of the three organs. A constitutional principle under the goal.
Rule by a few aristocratic families identified as oligarchy. Comparative government, with ancient Greece only as the setting.

Democracy preferred because it protects people's choices, freedoms and rights and lets them hold government to account. The value of equal rights carries the answer, so LO-175 rather than the bare goal.
A hereditary head of state with real power in an elected parliament has to be named a constitutional monarchy. Comparative government under the goal.
The Vajji and Lichchhavi assembly cited as an early republic. The chapter uses it as an ancestor of democratic practice, so the civics goal rather than the history administration outcome.
'Sovereign' as supreme authority free of external control. A constitutional term under the goal.
